title: Automated Logistics Manifest Processing
business: Logistics firms managing high-volume, multi-vendor shipping manifests.
problem: Manual reconciliation of vendor manifests against internal inventory records is error-prone and slows down warehouse throughput.
solution: Ruby's expressive syntax and powerful array manipulation capabilities allow developers to quickly build scripts that ingest vendor data, perform set operations to identify missing items, and generate clean reconciliation reports.
steps: Define a class to encapsulate manifest data and vendor-specific parsing logic.
Utilize Ruby's array subtraction operator to compare incoming vendor manifests against current warehouse inventory.
Implement data transformation methods to standardize vendor-provided item names.
Execute the reconciliation script to output a list of discrepancies for warehouse staff.
outcome: Increased accuracy in inventory tracking and reduced time spent on manual data verification.
limitation: Ruby's dynamic nature can lead to runtime errors if input data structures are inconsistent; developers must check for nil values or unexpected types during the parsing phase.

diagram.title: Manifest Reconciliation Workflow
diagram.description: The flow shows how raw vendor data is processed into actionable inventory insights.

code.content:
# Standardize incoming vendor items
vendor_items = ["Box-A", "Box-B", "Box-C"]
warehouse_stock = ["Box-A", "Box-C"]

# Identify missing items using array subtraction
missing = vendor_items - warehouse_stock

# Output results for reconciliation
puts "Missing items: #{missing.join(', ')}"
code.explanation: This code demonstrates the use of Ruby's array subtraction operator to identify discrepancies between vendor manifests and warehouse stock, directly addressing the reconciliation problem.
